​Building a 3D WebGL Mission Control for​
​Microservice Outages​
​When a major microservice architecture crashes, standard dashboards can feel​
​overwhelming. An on-call engineer is suddenly confronted with dozens of disconnected​
​browser tabs: Grafana graphs with spiking red lines, PagerDuty incidents, AWS CloudWatch​
​log streams, and Slack alert channels.​
​Trying to mentally map how a failure in an ingress API gateway cascades into a PostgreSQL​
​deadlock through raw text logs alone is difficult under pressure.​
​For​​MemOps SRE​, I wanted to build a visual control center that turns incident management​
​into an intuitive, spatial experience. Using Three.js and WebGL on the frontend, paired with​
​Server-Sent Events (SSE) from our FastAPI backend, we built an interactive 3D topology​
​mesh where services react physically to crashes, shockwaves ripple through dependencies,​
​and memory recall highlights proven paths to recovery.​
​Here is how we designed and implemented this live visual control plane, backed by​
​Hindsight agent memory​.​
​Designing Microservice Topology in 3D Space​
​Most infrastructure maps are static two-dimensional diagrams that quickly become out of​
​date. By rendering the microservice cluster directly in WebGL, we can represent health,​
​network traffic, and incident states through dynamic physical parameters:​
​●​ ​Node Color & Pulse:​​Healthy nodes glow emerald green. When an outage occurs,​
​the failing node bursts into a pulsing rose-red shockwave.​
​●​
​●​ ​Particle Streams:​​Animated particle lines connect dependent services (such as​
​Gateway to Auth, or Order to PostgreSQL), indicating active traffic flow.​
​●​
​●​ ​Memory Resonance:​​When our memory engine finds a historical match for an​
​outage, the node shifts to a warm gold/amber glow, indicating that a known solution​
​is available.​
​●​
​[API Gateway] (Cyan Ingress)​
​/                  \​
​v                    v​
​[Auth Node]           [Order Node] (Pulsing Red)​
​|                     |​
​v                     v​
​[Redis Cache]         [Postgres DB] (Golden Glow)​

​JavaScript​
​Building the WebGL Canvas with Three.js​
​Our 3D engine lives in​​visualizer3d.js​. It sets up​​an animated scene, an orbital camera, and​
​custom geometric nodes representing each microservice:​
​// frontend/visualizer3d.js​
​import​​* as THREE from​​'three'​;​
​export class​​MicroserviceMesh {​
​constructor​(canvasContainer) {​
​this​.container = canvasContainer;​
​this​.nodes = {};​
​this​.initScene();​
​}​
​initScene() {​
​this​.scene =​​new​​THREE.Scene();​
​this​.camera =​​new​​THREE.PerspectiveCamera(​60​,​​window.innerWidth /​
​window.innerHeight,​​0​.​1​,​​1000​);​
​this​.camera.position.set(​0​,​​5​,​​12​);​
​this​.renderer =​​new​​THREE.WebGLRenderer({​​antialias: true, alpha: true​
​});​
​this​.renderer.setSize(​this​.container.clientWidth,​
​this​.container.clientHeight);​
​this​.container.appendChild(​this​.renderer.domElement);​
​// Add soft ambient and directional lights​
​const​​ambientLight =​​new​​THREE.AmbientLight(​0xffffff​,​​0​.​6​);​
​this​.scene.add(ambientLight);​
​}​
​createServiceNode(​name​, x, y, z, colorHex =​​0x10b981​)​​{​
​const​​geometry =​​new​​THREE.SphereGeometry(​0​.​8​,​​32​,​​32​);​
​const​​material =​​new​​THREE.MeshStandardMaterial({​
​color: colorHex,​
​emissive: colorHex,​
​emissiveIntensity:​​0​.​4​,​
​roughness:​​0​.​2​
​});​
​const​​mesh =​​new​​THREE.Mesh(geometry, material);​
​mesh.position.set(x, y, z);​
​this​.scene.add(mesh);​
​this​.nodes[​name​] = { mesh, baseColor: colorHex,​​status:​​'healthy'​​};​
​}​
​}​

​The scene remains lightweight and runs smoothly at 60 frames per second directly in the​
​browser without requiring external graphics plugins.​
​Streaming Incident Events Over SSE​
​A visual interface is only as useful as the real-time data feeding it. Instead of forcing the​
​browser to poll the server every few seconds, our backend uses Server-Sent Events (SSE)​
​to push incident updates the millisecond they happen.​
​Here is the FastAPI streaming endpoint:​
​# app/main.py​
​import​​asyncio​
​from​​fastapi​​import​​FastAPI​
​from​​sse_starlette.sse​​import​​EventSourceResponse​
​app = FastAPI()​
​event_bus = asyncio.Queue()​
​@app.get(​"/api/v1/stream"​)​
​async def​​incident_event_stream():​
​async def​​event_generator():​
​while​​True:​
​event_data =​​await​​event_bus.get()​
​yield​​{​"event"​:​​"incident_update"​,​​"data"​:​​event_data}​
​return​​EventSourceResponse(event_generator())​
​On the frontend, our JavaScript client listens to the stream and immediately updates the 3D​
​topology:​
​// frontend/app.js​
​const​​eventSource =​​new​​EventSource(​'/api/v1/stream'​);​
​eventSource.addEventListener(​'incident_update'​, (e)​​=> {​
​const​​data =​​JSON​.parse(e.data);​
​if​​(data.type ===​​'OUTAGE_DETECTED'​) {​
​// Trigger pulsing red shockwave on the failing​​service node​
​visualizer.triggerOutageAnimation(data.service_name);​
​}​​else if​​(data.type ===​​'MEMORY_RECALLED'​) {​
​// Shift node to gold to signify an institutional​​memory match​
​visualizer.setNodeColor(data.service_name,​​0xf59e0b​);​
​displayHistoricalDiff(data.recalled_patch);​

​When an alert fires, the engineer sees the affected node light up in red instantly. Moments​
​later, as​​the Hindsight GitHub repository​​memory client​​matches the incident signature, the​
​node transitions to amber, and the historical diff opens in the panel below.​
​Integrating Unified Diff Inspection​
​A high-tech 3D visualizer is engaging, but engineers ultimately need to inspect code. Below​
​the 3D canvas, we built a unified diff reviewer that renders proposed patches with clear​
​syntax highlighting:​
​@@ -14,3 +14,3 @@​
​-    pool_size = 5​
​+    pool_size = 25​
​-    max_overflow = 0​
​+    max_overflow = 10​
​Beside the diff viewer, we display the confidence score and reference links based on the​
​specifications from the​​Hindsight documentation​.​
​The operator can inspect the 3D cluster, read the exact lines of code changing in the patch,​
​review the historical pull request, and click​​"Approve​​& Deploy Hotfix"​​without ever leaving​
​the screen.​

​Lessons Learned​
​1.​ ​Spatial visuals reduce cognitive load during incidents.​​Being able to see cluster​
​health in a single 3D view helps on-call engineers assess downstream impact much​
​faster than reading through terminal logs.​
​2.​ ​Server-Sent Events provide the ideal balance for SRE dashboards.​​SSE is vastly​
​simpler to implement and maintain than full WebSockets when your primary data flow​
​is one-way streaming from server to client.​
​3.​ ​Visuals must always connect to concrete code.​​A slick graphical interface is only​
​helpful if it leads directly to actionable code changes that resolve the problem at​
​hand.​

1. Project Title & Problem Statement 
Project Title: SchoolDocs - AI-Based Document Verification and Tamper Detection System for 
Education ERPs 
 
Problem Statement: During school/college admissions, scholarship applications, and campus 
placements, students upload thousands of documents such as marksheets, transfer certificates 
(TC), income certificates, and internship letters. Right now, Education ERPs and Job Portals 
only store these files and depend on staff or recruiters to open and check every single file 
manually. 
 
This creates three major problems: 
● Easy to Fake Documents: With free online PDF editors and photo editing tools, anyone 
can easily change a grade, CGPA, date, or signature on a marksheet in a few minutes. To 
the human eye, these edited files look completely real. 
● Huge Delays in Admissions and Placements: Checking thousands of student files one 
by one takes weeks for college office staff and HR teams, slowing down seat allotment 
and hiring. 
● High Background Check Costs: External verification agencies charge heavy fees per 
candidate and take 7 to 14 days, which schools and campus recruiters cannot afford for 
every student. 
 
2. Proposed Solution 
SchoolDocs is an automated document checking tool built to work directly inside a School 
ERP's Management Portal and Recruiter Portal. Instead of just saving uploaded files, our 
system scans every marksheet or certificate as soon as a student uploads it and tells the admin 
within 3 seconds if the document is genuine or edited. 
 
How It Works (Step-by-Step): 
 
1. Student Upload: The student uploads their marksheet, TC, or certificate (PDF, JPG, or 
PNG) on the portal. 
2. Three-Level Automated Check: 
○ Image Tampering Check: Uses OpenCV and Error Level Analysis (ELA) to check 
if specific pixels (like marks, roll numbers, or stamps) were edited and re-saved. 
○ PDF Metadata & Font Check: Uses PyMuPDF to read hidden file details. It checks 
if the PDF was modified using editing tools (like Photoshop, Canva, or iLovePDF) 
and detects if a different font was pasted over the original grades. 
○ Template & Marks Matching (RAG): Extracts the text using OCR, checks if the 
subject marks actually add up to the final total, and compares the document layout 
against original board/university templates stored in ChromaDB. 
3. Final Trust Score & Heatmap: The system gives an Authenticity Score (0% to 100%) 
along with a visual heatmap that highlights the exact edited area in red. 
4. Instant Portal Status: Documents scoring above 90% are marked "Verified" for admins 
and recruiters. Suspicious files are flagged for manual checking.

3. Key Features & Unique Value Proposition (UVP) 
Key Features: 
 
● Visual Tamper Heatmap: Shows admins the exact spot on a certificate where numbers 
or text were erased or overwritten. 
● Hidden PDF History Detection: Catches fake PDFs by checking hidden creation dates, 
editing software logs, and mismatched fonts. 
● Automatic Total & Grade Calculation: Reads subject marks via OCR and verifies that 
the total, percentage, and CGPA math is accurate. 
● Cross-Document Name Matching: Checks that the student's name, DOB, and parent 
details match across their Aadhaar card, marksheet, and TC. 
● Verified Badge for Recruiters: Gives companies on the Job Portal a pre-verified badge 
on student profiles so they can shortlist candidates with confidence. 
●  
Why Our Solution is Unique (UVP): Existing portals only act like Google Drive folders where 
admins still have to check files manually. Government tools like DigiLocker do not cover college 
internship certificates, local transfer certificates, or older scanned records. SchoolDocsAI works 
directly on normal scanned PDFs and photos, verifying documents in under 3 seconds at almost 
zero cost. 
 
4. Target Users & Expected Benefits 
● School & College Admins (Management Portal): Reduces manual document 
verification work by 80-85% during busy admission and scholarship seasons. 
● Campus Recruiters (Job Portal): Helps HR teams quickly filter and hire genuine 
candidates without worrying about fake internship letters or altered CGPA sheets. 
● Students (Student Portal): Honest students get faster admission approval and a 
"Verified Credentials" tag on their placement profile. 
5. Proposed Technology Stack 
 
● Frontend: Next.js, Tailwind CSS (Clean dashboard for admins to view trust scores and 
heatmaps) 
● Backend: Python, FastAPI (Fast API server to handle file uploads and processing) 
● Image & PDF Checking: OpenCV, Pillow (for Error Level Analysis), PyMuPDF (for PDF 
metadata and font checking), Tesseract OCR 
● AI & Database: ChromaDB (Vector database for matching original institutional templates 
via RAG), MongoDB (for storing verification logs) 
● Deployment: Docker, Vercel, Render

6. Innovation Concept & Potential Impact 
Innovation Concept: Instead of relying only on basic OCR (which reads fake text just like real 
text), SchoolDocs combines Computer Vision (pixel checking) + PDF Internal Structure 
Analysis + RAG Template Matching in one lightweight pipeline. It does not require schools or 
boards to change how they issue certificates. 
Real-World Impact: 
● Cuts admission and placement document verification time from weeks to just a few hours. 
● Stops fake marksheets, edited income certificates, and fake internship letters at the entry 
stage itself. 
● Can be plugged into any existing School ERP or Placement Portal as a simple API 
module.

# DATAOPS SOC I NOC IVAPT ## **INNOVATION HACKATHON** **AI-Powered Document Forensics and Contextual Intelligence System** ### **1. Background** Financial institutions and enterprises process large volumes of documents, including application forms, identity proofs, transaction requests, declarations, and supporting documents. Traditional document-processing systems primarily rely on Optical Character Recognition (OCR) to extract information and predefined validation rules to verify individual fields. However, extracting information does not necessarily establish whether the information is authentic, consistent, or reliable. Documents may contain subtle alterations, overwritten fields, inconsistent information, manipulated images, misplaced signatures, or discrepancies that become apparent only when multiple documents are examined together. Identifying such irregularities requires more than conventional OCR. It requires a system capable of understanding document structures, interpreting contextual information, examining visual characteristics, and establishing relationships between multiple sources of information. This challenge aims to develop an **AI-powered document intelligence and forensic investigation system** that goes beyond conventional text extraction to identify, investigate, and explain document-level anomalies. ### **2. Problem Statement** Design and develop an AI-powered Intelligent Document Forensics System capable of analyzing, interpreting, and investigating digital and scanned documents to identify suspicious modifications, contextual inconsistencies, and potential document manipulation. The proposed system must go beyond conventional OCR-based text extraction. It should combine document intelligence, computer vision, contextual analysis, and intelligent verification mechanisms to establish the reliability of information contained within submitted documents. Unlike conventional document verification systems that independently validate individual fields, the proposed solution should be capable of analyzing relationships between multiple documents, identifying discrepancies that may not be visible through isolated analysis, and investigating suspicious document characteristics. The system must demonstrate the ability to: Extract and interpret information from scanned and digital documents. Understand document layouts, structures, and relationships between fields. Identify suspicious modifications and visual inconsistencies. Correlate information across multiple related documents. Identify contextual discrepancies and potentially manipulated information. Generate evidence-backed explanations for identified anomalies. Maintain traceability between identified findings and their original document sources. The solution must demonstrate contextual understanding and evidence-driven investigation rather than relying exclusively on OCR output or predefined keyword-based rules. ### **3. Expected User Experience and End-to-End Flow** The proposed system should support the following end-to-end document investigation workflow: **Document Submission → Document Classification → OCR & Information Extraction → Structural Understanding → Visual Forensic Analysis → Contextual Verification → CrossDocument Correlation → Anomaly Investigation → Evidence Generation → Investigation Dossier** #### **Workflow Explanation** 1. **Document Submission:** Accept scanned documents, images, and digital documents as input. 2. **Document Classification:** Identify the document type and determine its structure and relevant information fields. 3. **OCR and Information Extraction:** Extract printed and handwritten information wherever applicable. 4. **Structural Understanding:** Organize extracted information into structured representations while preserving its relationship with the original document. 5. **Visual Forensic Analysis:** Examine document characteristics and identify suspicious modifications, overwritten fields, inconsistent fonts, image alterations, and other visual anomalies. 6. **Contextual Verification:** Examine relationships between extracted fields and identify inconsistencies within individual documents. 7. **Cross-Document Correlation:** Compare information across multiple related documents to identify conflicting or inconsistent records. 8. **Anomaly Investigation:** Analyse identified discrepancies and establish their supporting evidence. 9. **Evidence Generation:** Highlight suspicious regions and associate findings with the corresponding original document locations. 10. **Investigation Dossier:** Generate a structured report containing identified anomalies, supporting evidence, contextual explanations, and areas requiring further verification. The system should display processing progress, extracted information, identified anomalies, confidence levels, and supporting evidence. It should also clearly distinguish between observed visual characteristics, detected inconsistencies, and potential manipulation. ### **4. Technology Integration Scope** Participants may integrate technologies and frameworks from the following domains: |Technology / Domain|Primary Expected Role| |---|---| |OCR Engines|Extract printed and handwritten
information from documents.| |Computer Vision|Analyse document images and identify
visual irregularities.| |Image Processing|Examine image composition, alterations,
and suspicious regions.| |Document Layout Analysis|Identify document structures, sections,
tables, and fields.| |Natural Language Processing (NLP)|Interpret extracted information and
identify contextual inconsistencies.| |Large Language Models (LLMs)|Assist with contextual reasoning,
investigation explanations, and report
generation.| |Machine Learning / Deep Learning|Identify patterns and anomalies in
document information and visual
characteristics.| |Signature Analysis|Examine signature characteristics and their
placement within documents.| |Entity Matching|Establish relationships between
information extracted from multiple
documents.| Participants may use suitable open-source frameworks, pretrained models, APIs, and libraries. Teams must clearly document the technologies used, their respective roles, and the limitations of their implementations. ### **5. Functional Requirements** The proposed system must demonstrate the following functional capabilities. #### **5.1 Document Ingestion and Classification** - Accept scanned documents, images, and digital documents. - Support multiple documents within a single investigation. Identify document types and relevant document structures. Maintain document identifiers and source references. #### **5.2 OCR and Information Extraction** - Extract printed and handwritten information wherever applicable. Identify relevant fields, sections, and tables. - Convert extracted information into a structured representation. Maintain field-level confidence and references to original document locations. #### **5.3 Document Structure Understanding** - Identify relationships between different fields and sections. - Recognize document layouts and information hierarchies. - Identify missing, duplicated, or misplaced information. - Preserve the relationship between extracted information and its original location. #### **5.4 Visual Forensic Analysis** - Identify suspicious alterations and overwritten fields. - Examine inconsistencies in fonts, spacing, alignment, and document structure. Identify suspicious image insertions, replacements, or modifications. Analyse signatures and their placement within the document. Highlight potentially manipulated regions for further investigation. #### **5.5 Contextual Information Verification** - Identify inconsistencies between related fields within a document. Compare information across multiple submitted documents. Identify conflicting information and mismatched records. Detect missing, duplicated, or contextually inconsistent information. #### **5.6 Cross-Document Correlation** - Establish relationships between multiple documents belonging to the same application or transaction. - Compare extracted information across related documents. - Identify discrepancies that become visible only when multiple documents are analysed together. - Maintain traceability between related documents and their extracted information. #### **5.7 Evidence Mapping and Investigation** - Associate each identified anomaly with its original document. Highlight suspicious regions within the document. Provide supporting visual and textual evidence. Explain why a particular field or region requires further investigation. - Distinguish between confirmed observations and potential anomalies. #### **5.8 Investigation Dossier Generation** Generate a structured investigation dossier containing: - Document overview. - Extracted information. - Identified inconsistencies. - Visual forensic observations. - Cross-document discrepancies. - Supporting evidence. 1. Background
Financial institutions and enterprises process large volumes of documents, including 
application forms, identity proofs, transaction requests, declarations, and supporting 
documents.
Traditional document-processing systems primarily rely on Optical Character Recognition 
(OCR) to extract information and predefined validation rules to verify individual fields. 
However, extracting information does not necessarily establish whether the information is 
authentic, consistent, or reliable.
Documents may contain subtle alterations, overwritten fields, inconsistent information, 
manipulated images, misplaced signatures, or discrepancies that become apparent only when 
multiple documents are examined together.
Identifying such irregularities requires more than conventional OCR. It requires a system 
capable of understanding document structures, interpreting contextual information, 
examining visual characteristics, and establishing relationships between multiple sources of 
information.
This challenge aims to develop an AI-powered document intelligence and forensic 
investigation system that goes beyond conventional text extraction to identify, investigate, 
and explain document-level anomalies.

The solution should demonstrate its ability to understand document structures, examine 
visual characteristics, correlate information across multiple documents, identify contextual 
inconsistencies, and generate evidence-backed investigation findings.

The ultimate objective is to transform document processing from simple information 
extraction into intelligent, contextual, and evidence-driven document investigation.
